**In one line**: Music rights company Round Hill Music has filed separate copyright infringement lawsuits against AI music generator Suno and AI developer Anthropic.

### Key points
- Round Hill Music reportedly brought distinct legal actions targeting the two AI companies.
- The defendants are AI music generation service **Suno** and large language model developer **Anthropic**.
- The dispute appears to center on whether copyrighted material was used without authorization to train or generate AI output.
- The filings add to a growing wave of copyright litigation the music and publishing industries have brought against generative AI.

### Why it matters
By targeting both a music generator (Suno) and a text model developer (Anthropic), the suits signal that questions over AI training-data licensing are spreading beyond any single medium. The outcomes could shape how AI companies source training data and negotiate content licenses.
